newsitem.title: USA: Neiman seeks shr offer to buy back its stock.
newsitem.headline: Neiman seeks shr offer to buy back its stock.

text.p: The Neiman Marcus Group Inc said Wednesday it has filed a registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission for a public offering of eight million shares of its common stock, plus an underwriters' over-allotment option of 1.2 million shares. The company said it intends to use the net proceeds of the offering to partially fund a planned repurchase of all of its outstanding preferred stock for about $416 million, which it said represents 98 percent of the total stated value of its outstanding preferred stock, plus accrued and unpaid dividends.
The preferred stock is held by Harcourt General Inc, a majority shareholder of Neiman Marcus with common stock ownership of about 59 percent, Neiman said.

Neiman said payment for the preferred stock will consist of about $281 million in cash, plus accrued and unpaid dividends, and $135 million in shares of newly issued common stock in The Neiman Marcus Group, valued at the public offering price.
The transaction will eliminate the dividend requirements of the preferred stock, currently $27 million annually, the company said.
It said the deal will also eliminate future sinking fund requirements.
After the offering and repurchase, Harcourt General will remain the majority shareholder, holding at least 51 percent of the outstanding common equity, Neiman said.
